problem: Foundation-model (LLM) planners for robots hallucinate and are ambiguous about where objects are; existing FM-based maps (CLIP-Fields, VLMaps, ConceptGraphs) store semantics in feature space or require task specs, so they are neither human-verifiable/editable nor affordance-aware.
motivation: Robots in human environments need to plan navigation-manipulation tasks from natural language, but FMs guess among similar locations (e.g., many tables) and can hallucinate affordances. A compact, human-readable and editable map grounded in real locations can give assurance and let even small locally-deployable LLMs plan correctly.
key_idea: Represent the environment as a human-editable JSON topological graph whose semantic nodes (built from VLM descriptions of operator-chosen snapshots) list objects, affordances and ownership, and feed it with a skill API to a text-only LLM planner.
insight: Adding object-level semantic context to the map takes average task success across six LLMs from 38.9% to 100%, showing that most planning failures come from semantic ambiguity (which table? which drink?) rather than reasoning ability. Even Gemma 3 27B handles indirect queries and ownership-based tasks once the map contains object and ownership tags (Table 2), and human correction of the JSON removes VLM hallucination at planning time.
method: Topological graph: navigation nodes (free-space waypoints) with directed edges G(V,E), created as the operator walks the robot; a subset V_SE become semantic nodes.

Semantic nodes: at operator-chosen points of interest the robot takes an RGB snapshot; a Vision FM (Llama 3.2 90B Vision Instruct) fills a JSON template with entities (fridge, table), their manipulable state, and contained objects.
Human grounding: the operator inspects/edits the JSON to fix hallucinations and adds info such as ownership tags ("Bob's mug"), so the map is treated as ground truth.
Planning FM: a text-only LLM receives Scene JSON + skill API + robot physical constraints (e.g., single arm) + the natural-language query and outputs a skill sequence (following BUMBLE).
Execution: navigation nodes are used for global path planning, with off-the-shelf local collision avoidance and manipulation; a shortest-path planner between nodes is assumed.

setting.backbone: Vision FM: Llama 3.2 90B Vision Instruct (frozen) for map construction; planning LLMs (frozen): Llama 3.1 8B/405B, GPT-4o mini, o3 mini, Gemma 3 27B, Gemini 2.0 Flash
setting.observation: RGB snapshots at operator-selected nodes; human walkthrough for navigation graph
setting.action_space: discrete skill API over topological nodes (navigate to node, manipulation skills)
setting.privileged: human operator guidance and correction of the map (walkthrough, semantic node selection, JSON edits, ownership tags)

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark; custom small evaluation (3 object-retrieval tasks x 6 LLMs, plus 9 direct/indirect tasks on Gemma 3 27B) reported as checkmarks and percentages. Baseline avg 38.9% vs semantic enhancement 100% (Table 1).
results: On a 9-semantic-node, 23-object environment, semantic enhancement raised average task success across six LLMs from 38.9% (baseline, top-level locations only) to 100%, with every model succeeding on Get-Sponge/Coffee/Tissue. Gemma 3 27B solved all direct and indirect queries and ownership tasks with the enhanced map, while the baseline failed most indirect queries; Gemini 2.0 Flash refused all baseline tasks.
limitations: Requires substantial operator effort to annotate and does not scale to large environments; JSON may become long and hard for small LLMs or humans to parse.
Very small evaluation (one environment, three retrieval tasks, nine query tasks, binary success), no standard benchmarks or execution success reporting.
compares_to: Baseline Scene JSON without semantic enhancement (BUMBLE-style)
